purpose: Expands WP-CLI integration from 4 to 12 subcommands, adding cache preload/status, database optimize/counts, image convert/status, settings export/import, object-cache management, pagespeed scans, and system-info retrieval — all delegating to existing backend methods.
riskRationale: All changes are in WP-CLI-only code paths requiring manage_options capability. Backend methods already exist and are well-tested. No data flows through new REST endpoints or UI components. The issues found are localized error-handling gaps (false-positive success messages) and a batch-size discrepancy — all straightforward to fix.

text: Solid PR that follows established codebase patterns with clean delegation to existing backend methods. Three important issues need fixing: (1) Pagespeed queue_scan always reports success even when Action Scheduler is unavailable, (2) database cleanup methods returning false are silently cast to 0 and reported as success, and (3) image conversion lacks batch limiting while the cron equivalent caps at 50. Two minor issues around non-recursive cache stats counting and silent WP_Error skipping in clean_all() should also be addressed.

reasoning: Three important error-handling gaps need fixing: false-positive success messages for Pagespeed and database cleanup, and a missing batch-size cap on image conversion. All are straightforward, localized fixes to the CLI command class with no architectural concerns.

message: Path traversal protection via realpath() + ABSPATH prefix check on image source paths is well-implemented — resolves symlinks before the prefix test, preventing escape from the WordPress root.

Sensitive data handling in settings export/import is thorough: export strips Redis password and PageSpeed API key; import converts password to a password_set boolean flag. This prevents credential leakage through CLI output or shared files.
All subcommands follow the existing @when after_wp_load, @subcommand, and positional $args[0] action pattern consistently, making the code easy to navigate and extend.
Pagespeed::queue_scan() returns 0 when Action Scheduler is unavailable, but the CLI always reports success with Job ID: 0, misleading the user into thinking a scan was queued.
suggestion: Check if the returned job_id is > 0 before reporting success. If 0, show an error indicating Action Scheduler is unavailable.

message: Database cleanup methods (clean_revisions, clean_auto_drafts, etc.) return int|false where false indicates a query failure. The code only checks is_wp_error() but not false, so a failing cleanup is silently converted to 0 and reported as success (0 items removed).
suggestion: Add an explicit false check after the WP_Error check. If the method returns false, show an error instead of a success message.

message: Image conversion processes ALL pending images synchronously without batch limiting, while the cron equivalent in class-cron.php defaults to a batch size of 50. This deviation from claimed matching cron behavior could cause timeout or memory exhaustion on sites with hundreds/thousands of pending images.
suggestion: Apply the same batch-size limit from settings (options['image_optimisation']['batch'] ?? 50) and report the batch count to the user, or document the synchronous-all behavior as intentional.

message: Cache::get_cache_stats() counts cached_pages via dirlist on the domain root directory without recursion. Nested paths (e.g., /category/post/) are undercounted — only the parent directory is tallied. This is a display-only metric for CLI status, but it is systematically inaccurate for sites with nested URL structures.
suggestion: Walk the directory tree recursively to count all index.html files as individual cached pages, or document the limitation that this is a top-level directory count.

message: Database clean_all() results silently skip WP_Error entries in the foreach loop, providing no warning that individual cleanup types failed. The user sees a success message with a reduced total and no indication of errors.
suggestion: Log a warning via WP_CLI::warning() for each WP_Error result before continuing, so the user knows which cleanup types failed.
